gear.description: A typical blanket for keeping warm on cold nights.

gear.name: Bong
gear.description: A portable hookah for inhaling recreational smoke. This could also be a vape pen, a rechargeable mini-hookah that uses fluid tablets to produce smoke.

gear.name: Burner phone
gear.description: The “dumb” version of a smartphone. It can do most of the things a smartphone can do, but worse. Its major advantage is not needing your personal information to work, and not being traceable to you.

gear.name: Canteen
gear.description: A half-gallon container for holding water or booze.

gear.name: Chain (10 ft)
gear.description: A length of metal chain. Useful for connecting heavy objects, chaining up enemies, or beating the shit out of people. The price is per 10ft of length.

gear.name: Climbing kit
gear.description: A climbing kit includes special pitons, boot tips, gloves, and a harness. You can use the climbing kit as an action to anchor yourself; when you do, you can't fall more than 25 feet from the point where you anchored yourself, and you can't climb more than 25 feet away from that point without undoing the anchor.

gear.name: Component pouch
gear.description: A component pouch is a small, watertight belt pouch that has compartments to hold all the material requirements and other special items you need to cast your techs, except for those components that have a specific cost (as indicated in a tech’s description).

gear.name: Crowbar
gear.description: Using a crowbar grants advantage to Strength checks where the crowbar’s leverage can be applied.

gear.name: Cyberdeck
gear.description: A compact but powerful personal computer. The typical cyberdeck looks like a black cube or rectangle about 6 to 12 inches in length. It can be accessed wirelessly by a user’s peripherals, but serious users utilize a physical connection to their datajack for improved speeds. Techwizards need a cyberdeck to store their tech programs.

gear.name: Drugs, euphoric
gear.description: Euphoric drugs induce a sense of happiness and connection to the world, granting advantage on Charisma checks and saving throws against fear, but disadvantage on Intelligence and Wisdom checks. The effects last 1 hour.

gear.name: Drugs, relaxant
gear.description: Relaxants make the user lethargic and sleepy, giving them advantage on saving throws against effects based on negative emotions (like fear and anger) but disadvantage on saving throws against sleep-based effects and concentration checks. A renegade under the effects of a relaxant cannot get hype. The effects last for 1 hour.

gear.name: Drugs, stimulant
gear.description: Stimulants make the user jumpy, nervous, and full of energy, granting advantage on initiative checks and saving throws against sleep-based effects, but disadvantage on Wisdom checks and saving throws against fear. The effects last 1 hour.

gear.name: Executive ring
gear.description: An expensive ring showing the wearer’s allegiance to a given corporation, typically given to middle managers and low-ranking corpos. Higher-ranked corpos have more expensive rings, typically with integrated electronics.

gear.name: Eyedrops
gear.description: As an action, you may apply eyedrops to your eyes. For the next 10 minutes after application, you do not suffer disadvantage on sight-based skill checks due to exhaustion (such as Wisdom (Perception) to spot something with your eyes, or an Intelligence check made with hacking tools to notice a change in some written code). A typical bottle of eyedrops has enough liquid for ten uses.

gear.name: Fishing pole
gear.description: A pole for fishing. Self-explanatory.

gear.name: Flare
gear.description: A flare is a single-use light source. It burns for 1 hour, providing bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. If you make a melee attack with a lit flare and hit, it deals 1 fire damage.

gear.name: Flashlight
gear.description: This hand-held light creates a cone of bright light for 60 feet and dim light for an additional 60 feet. A minute of cranking powers it for an hour.

gear.name: Flask
gear.description: A hip flask to hold a pint of hard liquor.

gear.name: Footlocker
gear.description: A small trunk that can hold 12 cubic feet or 300 pounds of gear. Needs a lock to actually be secure.

gear.name: Grappling hook
gear.description: A metal hook intended to be used with a length of rope. You throw the grappling hook up to catch onto a ledge, then climb the rope. Easy peasy.

gear.name: Hammer
gear.description: A simple tool with a weighted head for driving nails or breaking small objects. Can be used as an improvised baton.

gear.name: Holoprojector
gear.description: Most people just use these to watch holographic movies, but a shut-in can soup it up to act as a mobile projector for their avatar and use it as a tech focus.

gear.name: Ladder
gear.description: This portable ladder folds up to a little over a foot long when not in use. Unfolded, it is 10 feet long.

gear.name: Lantern
gear.description: A rechargeable portable electric lamp. It casts bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. It lasts 6 hours on a full charge and takes about 10 minutes to fully recharge if plugged into a power outlet, or about an hour if left in direct sunlight.

gear.name: Lighter
gear.description: A rechargeable lighter to start small fires.

gear.name: Lock, biometric
gear.description: An electronic lock that is keyed to someone's biometric data. Without one of the normal ways of accessing the lock, a creature proficient with hacker's kits can pick this lock with a successful DC 19 Intelligence check. Better locks are available at higher prices.

gear.name: Lock, keycard
gear.description: An electronic lock keyed to open with keycards. Without one of the normal ways of accessing the lock, a creature proficient with hacker's kits can pick this lock with a successful DC 15 Intellligence check. Better locks are available at higher prices.

gear.name: Lock, mechanical
gear.description: A mechanical lock that requires a physical key. Without one of the normal ways of accessing the lock, a creature proficient with locksmith’s tools can pick this lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Better locks are available at higher prices.

gear.name: Lock, pick-resistant
gear.description: A mechanical lock that requires two physical pick-resistant keys in tandem. Without one of the normal ways of accessing the lock, a creature proficient with locksmith’s tools can pick this lock with a successful DC 19 Dexterity check. Better locks are available at higher prices.

gear.name: Lock, twofactor
gear.description: A combination mechanical and electronic lock that is synced to both basic biometric data and a physical key. Without both of the normal ways of accessing the lock, a creature proficient with both hacker’s kits and locksmith's tools can pick this lock with both a successful DC 17 Intelligence check and a successful DC 17 Dexterity check, made within two rounds of each other.

gear.name: Mealbar
gear.description: A single day’s worth of nutrition in a fairly flavorless emergency ration block. Unless you buy it from somewhere that actually makes tasty ones. Those might cost a little more.

gear.name: Mess kit
gear.description: This metal box contains a cup and simple cutlery. The box clamps together, and one side can be used as a cooking pan and the other as a plate or shallow bowl. Useful for camping, living rough, or making meals on the go.

gear.name: M.U.L.E.
gear.description: The Mass Utility Labor Engine is a multi-legged robotic lockbox capable of carrying the spoils of any freelancer’s hoard while they are busy. The M.U.L.E. has a carrying capacity of 500 pounds and can follow simple directions, either verbally or by an app on the owner’s personal device. It cannot fight but will run if attacked.

gear.name: Quiver
gear.description: A long tube to hold arrows. Can hold up to 20 arrows.

gear.name: Restraints
gear.description: These high-strength shackles can bind a Small or Medium creature. Escaping the restraints requires a successful DC 20 Dexterity check. Breaking them requires a successful DC 20 Strength check. Each set of restraints comes with one key. Without the key, a creature proficient with locksmith’s tools can pick the restraints’ lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Restraints have 15 hit points.

gear.name: Rope (50 ft)
gear.description: Typically made of nylon or paracord, rope is useful for a lot of things. It has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check. The listed price is for a length of 50 feet of rope.

gear.name: Shovel
gear.description: Useful for digging holes or excavating collapsed tunnels in old ruins.

gear.name: Smartphone
gear.description: A typical consumer-model personal communication device. Can make calls, send texts, play games, and connect to the net. Also used for personal identification purposes and purchases if linked to your biometric data—and why wouldn’t you do that unless you have something to hide?

gear.name: Smartwatch
gear.description: A wrist timepiece that can also make calls and send texts. Typically linked to your biometric data the same way a smartphone would be. Can be paired with a smartphone to extend both devices' features.

gear.name: Spray paint (1 can)
gear.description: A can of aerosol paint used for street art or graffiti. Comes in a wide variety of colors.

gear.name: Streaming kit
gear.description: A personal array of recording devices that can wirelessly connect to the net in order to broadcast your activities to others. Typically includes a camera, microphone, halo light, and editing software.

gear.name: Suitcase
gear.description: A convenient, zippered container with wheels on the bottom. A suitcase can hold up to 1 cubic foot or 30 pounds of stuff.

gear.name: Tablet
gear.description: A personal computing device with an 8- to 10-inch touchscreen. Used for reading, playing games, and watching videos more than for communication purposes, but can also send emails and make calls if it has an attached data plan.

gear.name: Tech focus
gear.description: A special peripheral customized by a techcaster to connect all of their other peripherals together and make them work more efficiently.

gear.name: Tent
gear.description: A simple and portable shelter. Sleeps two people if they’re very friendly.

gear.name: UV lamp
gear.description: A portable lamp that converts electricity into low-powered ultraviolet light. Suitable for growing a potted plant or recharging a solar-powered device (or person) in the absence of real sunlight. Basically, these are just annoying to Hacked and other creatures who are damaged by sunlight.

gear.name: Water purifier
gear.description: This siphon and container allow you to turn 1 gallon of tainted or salt water into 1 gallon of drinkable water. It requires exposure to sunlight for 6 hours or being hooked into a portable battery for 1 hour. The filters need cleaning every 10 gallons or so.

gear.name: Wrist nanobot dispenser
gear.description: Like a smartwatch on steroids. Useful for enforcers to direct their techs and control their special augments, but overkill for almost anyone else.

gear.name: Arrows (20)
gear.description: An arrow is a fin-stabilized projectile launched by a bow. A typical arrow usually consists of a long, stiff, straight shaft with a weighty (and usually sharp and pointed) arrowhead attached to the front end, multiple fin-like stabilizers called fletchings mounted near the rear, and a slot at the rear end called a nock for engaging the bowstring. This is a pack of 20 non-technical arrows.

gear.name: Bullets, pistol (20)
gear.description: A bullet is a kinetic projectile, a component of firearm ammunition that is shot from a gun barrel. These are primarily made of steel and lead. Pistol rounds are a lower caliber, usually, such as 9mm or .380. They also generally contain less powder. This is a pack of 20 non-technical bullets.

gear.name: Bullets, rifle (20)
gear.description: A bullet is a kinetic projectile, a component of firearm ammunition that is shot from a gun barrel. These are primarily made of steel and lead. Rifle rounds are a higher caliber, usually, such as the still-in-use 7.62x39mm (or 7.62mm Soviet), or the 5.56x45mm NATO round. They also generally contain more powder. This is a pack of 20 non-technical bullets.

gear.name: Pellets, slingshot (20)
gear.description: A slingshot pellet is basically an oversized ball bearing that's been polished smooth and made of a relatively heavier material to ensure additional damage upon impact. They're still much lighter to carry than regular ammo, owing to the lack of cartridges or powder. This is a pack of 20 non-technical pellets.

gear.name: Shells, shotgun (20)
gear.description: A shotgun shell, shotshell or simply shell is a type of rimmed, cylindrical cartridges used specifically in shotguns, and is typically loaded with numerous small, pellet-like spherical sub-projectiles called buckshot. A shell can sometimes also contain only a single large solid projectile known as a slug, fired usually through a rifled slug barrel. This is a pack of 20 non-technical shells, which can be either slugs or buckshot.

gear.name: Corpo pack
gear.description: This pack contains a suitcase, sleep mask, traveling blanket, lighter, tablet, a nice suit or dress, 2 days of mealbars, a canteen, and 2 doses of stimulant drugs.

gear.name: Delver's pack
gear.description: This pack contains a backpack, crowbar, hammer, climbing kit, flashlight, mess kit, 10 days of mealbars, canteen, water purifier and 50 feet of rope.

gear.name: Edgerunner's pack
gear.description: This pack contains a backpack, crowbar, hammer, three UV flares, two cans of spray paint, set of restraints, flashlight, 5 days of mealbars, canteen, water purifier and 50 feet of rope.

gear.name: Hacker's pack
gear.description: This pack contains a suitcase, tablet, cyberdeck, bottle of eyedrops, and 2 doses of stimulant drugs or relaxant drugs.

gear.name: Hobo's pack
gear.description: This pack contains a backpack, bedroll, mess kit, lighter, flashlight, 10 days of mealbars, canteen, and either a tent or 50 feet of rope.

gear.name: Nightclubber's pack
gear.description: This pack contains a satchel or big purse, overnight kit, disguise kit, two club outfits, flashlight, 5 days of mealbars, canteen, pepper spray, and 1 dose of a euphoric drug.

gear.name: Salesperson's pack
gear.description: This pack contains a suitcase, waterproof plastic zip-folder for documents, nice suit or dress, tablet, flashlight, disguise kit, shaving kit, perfume or cologne, and pepper spray.

gear.name: Vandal's pack
gear.description: This pack contains a backpack, a bag of marbles or ball bearings, 10 feet of string, signal whistle, flashlight, crowbar, hammer, 5 flares, 1 incendiary grenade, 5 days of mealbars, lighter, 1 can of spray paint, canteen, and 50 feet of rope.

gear.name: Armorer's Tools
gear.description: This toolcase is used to build and repair armor. It include hammers, a fire starter, screwdrivers, tongs, charcoal, rags, and a whetstone. These tools allow you to work metal, heating it to alter its shape, repair damage, or work raw metal into useful items.

gear.name: Artist's Supplies
gear.description: A canvas bag, pun intended, containing supplies necessary for the discipline of the visual arts. It contains brushes, inks, paints, pencils, drawing tablets, and other implements to create visual art.

gear.name: Basic Toolkit
gear.description: A small set of miniaturized tools useful for basic tinkering and minor repairs.

gear.name: Board game set
gear.description: A board game set can encompass a wide variety of games that are specifically played on a board. This primarily includes games that have pieces that aren't interchangeable and have specific rules towards playing it. Real life variations would include games like Settlers of Catan or Monopoly.

gear.name: Builder's Tools
gear.description: This rough, no-frills case contains hammers, drills, levels, stud finders, and similar heavy tools for construction and architecture.

gear.name: Cook's Utensils
gear.description: A knapsack containing spoons, measuring cups, pans, pots, small knives, and other items useful for the preparation of tasty, home-cooked food.

gear.name: Dice set
gear.description: A dice set is, well, a set of dice. They can be many different kinds: a full RPG set (including a d20, d12, 2 d10s for percentile, a d8, a d6 and a d4), a little collection of six d6s, or any variation you might like. Many different games can be played with a dice set: Liar's Dice, Yahtzee, etc. and a user proficient with this set is assumed to be proficient in them.

gear.name: Disguise kit
gear.description: This pouch of cosmetics, hair dye, and small props lets you create disguises that change your physical appearance.

gear.name: Electrician's Tools
gear.description: A reinforced metal box containing voltmeters, wire snips, screwdrivers, pliers, soldering guns, circuit diagrams, and other tools used to work with electricity.

gear.name: First aid kit
gear.description: A small box containing bandages, sutures, ointments, and low-grade painkillers. Used to stabilize dying characters and perform minor medical procedures.

gear.name: Hacker's Kit
gear.description: A palmtop computer, a variety of data sticks with anti-security programs, a black box VPN solution, and other electronic devices used to gain illicit access to private networks and encrypted data.

gear.name: Jeweler's Tools
gear.description: A chic pouch containing tiny screwdrivers, chisels, hammers, pliers, lenses, and other items to make fine jewelry.

gear.name: Locksmith's Tools
gear.description: This set of tools includes lockpicks, files, pliers, tiny screwdrivers, bypass clips, and other small implements useful for defeating physical and electronic security. These tools can also be used to disarm traps.

gear.name: Mechanic's Tools
gear.description: This toolcase contains ratchets, wrenches, compression testers, ball bearings, lubricant, and other tools necessary to work on mechanical devices.

gear.name: Microbrewing Kit
gear.description: A case carrying bottles, stoppers, growlers, proof testers, yeast cultures, and items needed to brew booze from scratch.

gear.name: Microlab
gear.description: A small box containing a high-powered microscope, vials, chemicals, reagents, and other implements useful to create toxins, antitoxins, and targeted vaccines.

gear.name: Musical Instrument
gear.description: These tools are used to produce music. Each category of musical instruments is its own proficiency. Some of the more common musical categories include: bowed string, electronic, keyboard, percussion, plucked string, vocal, and wind instruments.

gear.name: Playing cards
gear.description: A playing card set is a deck of playing cards. It can be many different kinds: a tarot deck, a standard 52-card deck, or more. Many different kinds of games can be played with these, and having proficiency with playing cards assumes one has skill in most, if not all, of those games.

gear.name: Programmer's Kit
gear.description: A small case containing microcontrollers, LCD screens, micro-sensors, cables, light strips, electronic reference manuals, and similar necessities for programming and reprogramming computer-controlled devices.

gear.name: Scammer's Kit
gear.description: This small box contains a variety of papers, inks, seals, digital spoofers, and other supplies necessary to create convincing forgeries of physical documents and digital identification.

gear.name: Tailor's Tools
gear.description: A well-kept container holding scissors, needles, thread, tape measures, body scanners, and other useful gear for making stylish clothes.

gear.name: Trailblazer's Kit
gear.description: A side bag containing a compass, a set of binoculars, a sextant, a global positioning unit, digital maps, and other tools useful for keeping track of your location.

gear.name: Weaponsmith's Tools
gear.description: This toolcase contains whetstone, tiny screwdrivers, extra springs, gun oil, files, wire brushes, and the necessities for making, repairing, and maintaining implements of death.
